Name: One requisition, one candidate record
Statement: Every hiring need and every person in the funnel has one authoritative record from approval to hire.
Implications: Retire parallel ATS and trackers; one requisition ID and one candidate ID.

Name: Process before tool
Statement: Agree the standard hiring process first, then configure; vary only where law or a role family demands it.
Rationale: Automating a broken process locks in the problem.
Implications: Fit-to-standard workshops before configuration; local variants are recorded decisions.

Name: Candidate experience is a design input
Statement: Every step is mobile-first, accessible, multilingual and honest about status.
Rationale: Drop-off and brand damage cost more than the tooling.
Implications: Candidate journey tested in each language; survey after each stage.

Name: Humans decide
Statement: AI and automated scoring advise recruiters and managers; people make every selection and rejection decision.
Rationale: Law, ethics and trust in hiring.
Implications: Human review logged for each decision; no auto-reject on a score alone.

Name: Candidate data is held in trust
Statement: Collect the minimum, with consent and purpose; keep it only as long as the law and the business need.
Implications: Retention per country; auto-anonymise; consent records kept.

Name: Canonical hiring model
Statement: Partners map to OmniVerse's canonical entities and codes; partner formats never become the enterprise model.
Implications: Canonical data model; mapping tables in the integration hub.

Name: Summary, not raw sensitive detail
Statement: Sensitive screening detail stays with the specialist provider; the hiring system holds status and decision only.
Rationale: Reduces breach impact and legal exposure.
Implications: Check results stored as outcome and date; reports via vendor portal with audit.

Name: Every entity has an owner and steward
Statement: Named roles own definitions, quality and access for each data domain.
Implications: Data council; owners recorded in data_entities.

Name: Hub and spokes
Statement: One talent acquisition hub; partners attach to the hub, never to each other.
Rationale: Keeps integration count linear, not quadratic.
Implications: No partner-to-partner links; all through the integration hub.

Name: Buy, configure, then extend
Statement: Use standard capability first; extend on the integration or extension platform only for a proven gap.
Implications: Gap needs a documented fit-gap and an ADR.

Name: Capability interface, replaceable partner
Statement: Each partner category is consumed through a defined capability interface with an adapter.
Implications: Adapter per partner; contract test pack per category.

Name: Event-driven by default
Statement: Status changes flow as events (webhooks); batch only for bulk and reporting.
Implications: Webhook receiver, retry and dead-letter handling.

Name: Open standards
Statement: REST/JSON, OAuth 2.0, SAML/OIDC, SCIM and webhooks with signed payloads.

Name: Zero trust for partners
Statement: Every partner gets scoped, rotatable credentials, least privilege and logged calls.
Rationale: Third-party risk is the largest attack surface.
Implications: Secrets vault; per-partner scopes; quarterly access review.

Name: Residency and sovereignty by design
Statement: Data stays in approved regions; regional controls and processing locations are configured and evidenced.
Implications: Region map per partner; transfer impact assessments.

Name: Observable and exit-ready
Statement: Every integration is monitored; every partner has a tested exit and data-return plan.
Implications: Dashboards, alerts, exit runbooks, annual exit test for critical partners.
